mainTopic: דוד's forgiveness, the stories of גחזי and יהושע בן פרחיה with the lesson of not pushing away with both hands, and the משנה on generations with no share in עולם הבא.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a proof that דוד had צרעת for six months, and then tells how his forgiveness became public. When שלמה brought the ארון into the בית המקדש, the gates stayed shut until he mentioned דוד's kindnesses. The גמרא then turns to גחזי, one of the people the משנה says has no share in עולם הבא. אלישע tried to bring him back to תשובה, but גחזי said that one who causes the many to sin is not given the chance to repent. The גמרא offers three opinions about what he did, and tells how he took נעמן's gifts and was struck with צרעת. A ברייתא teaches that the left hand should push away while the right hand draws close. The story of יהושע בן פרחיה and ישו shows what happens when this is not followed. After a list of 'firsts' (old age with אברהם, illness with יעקב, recovery with אלישע), a new משנה begins about דור המבול, דור הפלגה and אנשי סדום losing עולם הבא. It ends with רבי נחמיה's disagreement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Six months missing from דוד's reign show he had צרעת
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים give different lengths for דוד's reign in חברון. The extra six months are left out of his total reign, which proves he was struck with צרעת during that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says: 'In חברון he reigned seven years, and in ירושלים he reigned thirty-three years.' Another פסוק says: 'In חברון he reigned over יהודה seven years and six months.' The first פסוק does not count those six months. Learn from this that he had צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that began just before this section. It points out that six months of דוד's reign are 'missing' from the official count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלכים א counts דוד's reign as forty years: seven in חברון and thirty-three in ירושלים. שמואל ב says he was in חברון seven and a half years. The גמרא explains that the extra six months were not counted as real kingship because he had צרעת then, and a מצורע lives apart from others.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. It introduces the conclusion drawn from a source.
He was struck with צרעת (a skin affliction).
And it is written. It introduces a second פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: This section begins in the middle of a פסוק. The opening words of מלכים א 2:11 ('and the days that דוד reigned were forty years') came just before this.

phrases.english: "In Hebron he reigned seven years
and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years"
And it is written: "In Hebron he reigned over Judah
seven years and six months, etc."
And these six months, he does not count.
Learn from this: he was afflicted with leprosy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof (begun before this section) that דוד was a מצורע for six months.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that דוד had צרעת for six months.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The difference between מלכים א 2:11 (seven years) and שמואל ב 5:5 (seven years and six months).

steps.title: דוד asks forgiveness and is forgiven
steps.stepSummary: דוד asks הקדוש ברוך הוא to forgive his sin, and הקדוש ברוך הוא tells him it is forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said before Him: Master of the World, forgive me for that sin! He answered: It is forgiven for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: after his suffering, דוד asks for forgiveness and is told he is forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forgiveness itself is granted right away. What is still missing, as the next step shows, is any public proof of it. This sets up דוד's request for a sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World. A way of addressing הקדוש ברוך הוא in prayer.

phrases.english: He said before Him:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מְחוֹל לִי עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן!
phrases.english: Master of the World, forgive me for that sin!
phrases.notes: "That sin" is the one the גמרא was just discussing, the story of בת שבע.

phrases.english: It is forgiven for you.
phrases.notes: Now הקדוש ברוך הוא is answering. The גמרא skips the words "He said".

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מְחוֹל לִי עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his punishment of צרעת, דוד seeks forgiveness.

steps.title: דוד asks for a public sign, which is promised for שלמה's time
steps.stepSummary: דוד asks for a visible sign so his enemies will see he was forgiven. הקדוש ברוך הוא says it will not happen in דוד's lifetime, only in the lifetime of his son שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said: 'Make a sign for good for me, so that those who hate me will see it and be ashamed, because You, ה׳, helped me and comforted me.' He said to him: In your lifetime I will not make it known, but I will make it known in the lifetime of your son שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד wants more than private forgiveness. He wants people to see it. הקדוש ברוך הוא agrees, but delays the sign until שלמה's time, which sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד uses a פסוק from תהלים as his request. The answer creates a promise that the next story fulfills: the sign will appear during שלמה's reign.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign for good, a visible sign of favor.

phrases.english: "Make with me a sign for good,
so those who hate me will see and be ashamed,
because You, God, helped me and comforted me."
He said to him: In your lifetime I will not make it known,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֲנִי מוֹדִיעַ בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה בִּנְךָ.
phrases.english: but I will make it known in the lifetime of Solomon your son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the forgiveness: דוד now asks for it to be made public.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sign of דוד's forgiveness will be shown in שלמה's lifetime, not in דוד's.

steps.title: The בית המקדש gates stay shut despite שלמה's prayers
steps.stepSummary: When שלמה tried to bring the ארון into the קדשי הקדשים, the gates stuck together. Twenty-four prayers, including the פסוקים of 'Lift up your heads, O gates,' did not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שלמה built the בית המקדש, he wanted to bring the ארון into the קדשי הקדשים. The gates stuck to each other. He said twenty-four songs of prayer and was not answered. He said: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Who is this King of glory? ה׳, strong and mighty, ה׳, mighty in battle.' And it says: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, lift them up, everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in,' and still he was not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the story of how the promise to דוד was fulfilled. First it shows that all of שלמה's own prayers failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long list of failed prayers matters for the story. It shows that שלמה's own praise was not enough to open the gates. That way, when the gates finally open, it is clear that only דוד's merit did it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: At the time Solomon built the Temple,
he wanted to bring in the Ark
into the Holy of Holies.
The gates stuck to each other.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה רְנָנוֹת וְלֹא נַעֲנָה.
phrases.english: He said twenty-four songs of prayer and was not answered.
He said: "Lift up your heads, O gates,
and be lifted up, everlasting doors,
and the King of glory will come in.
Who is this King of glory?

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ עִזּוּז וְגִבּוֹר ה׳ גִּבּוֹר מִלְחָמָה״.
phrases.english: God, strong and mighty; God, mighty in battle."
And it says: "Lift up your heads, O gates,
and lift them up, everlasting doors,
and the King of glory will come in, etc."
and he was not answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the story that fulfills the promise made in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה's own many prayers could not open the gates.

steps.title: Mentioning דוד opens the gates and shows he was forgiven
steps.stepSummary: Only when שלמה asked הקדוש ברוך הוא to remember the kindnesses of דוד did the gates open. דוד's enemies were shamed, and all ישראל knew he had been forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he said: 'ה׳ אלהים, do not turn away the face of Your anointed one; remember the kindnesses of דוד Your servant,' he was answered right away. At that moment the faces of דוד's enemies turned dark like the bottom of a pot, and all ישראל knew that הקדוש ברוך הוא had forgiven him for that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its end: דוד's merit opens the gates, and this is the public sign that was promised to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After twenty-four failed prayers, it worked only when דוד was mentioned. That made it clear to everyone that דוד was still beloved before הקדוש ברוך הוא. This fulfills דוד's request in step 3 that his enemies 'see and be ashamed.'

keyTerms.meaning: The bottom of a pot, blackened from the fire.

steps.whatToRemember: דוד had צרעת for six months as a punishment and was privately forgiven. The public proof came only in שלמה's time, when the בית המקדש gates opened in דוד's merit and his enemies were shamed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that דוד's forgiveness was complete and that his merit stayed powerful even after his death.

phrases.english: Once he said:
"Lord God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed one;
remember the kindnesses of David Your servant,"
he was answered right away.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה נֶהְפְּכוּ פְּנֵי שׂוֹנְאֵי דָּוִד
phrases.english: At that moment the faces of David's enemies turned
like the bottom of a pot,
and all Israel knew

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּחַל לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל אוֹתוֹ הֶעָוֹן.
phrases.english: that the Holy One, Blessed be He, had forgiven him for that sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמַר: ה׳ אֱלֹהִים אַל תָּשֵׁב פְּנֵי מְשִׁיחֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the failed prayers of step 4 and fulfills the promise of step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The gates opened only in דוד's merit, publicly proving to all ישראל that הקדוש ברוך הוא had forgiven דוד's sin.

steps.title: אלישע goes to דמשק to bring גחזי back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts discussing גחזי. Using a פסוק, רבי יוחנן explains that אלישע traveled to דמשק to bring גחזי back to תשובה, but גחזי did not return.
steps.simpleTranslation: גחזי, as it is written: 'And אלישע went to דמשק.' Where did he go? רבי יוחנן says: He went to bring גחזי back in תשובה, but גחזי did not repent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next person in the משנה's list, גחזי. It explains that his teacher אלישע went all the way to דמשק to try to bring him back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only that אלישע went to דמשק and gives no reason. The גמרא asks why, and רבי יוחנן answers that the purpose was to make גחזי do תשובה. The attempt failed, which sets up the next step, where we learn why.

keyTerms.meaning: The attendant (servant-student) of the prophet אלישע
To bring someone back through repentance

phrases.english: Gehazi, as it is written:
"And Elisha went to Damascus."
Where did he go (and why)?
Rabbi Yochanan says:
He went to bring Gehazi back in repentance,
but he did not repent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of דוד to a new figure from the משנה's list, גחזי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלישע went to דמשק to bring גחזי to תשובה, but גחזי did not repent.

steps.title: גחזי explains why he cannot repent
steps.stepSummary: אלישע tells גחזי to repent. גחזי answers by quoting אלישע's own teaching: one who sins and causes the many to sin is not given the chance to repent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלישע said to him: Repent. גחזי said to him: This is what I received from you: One who sins and causes the many to sin is not given the chance to repent.
steps.whatsHappening: We hear the actual conversation. גחזי refuses, and he uses his own teacher's lesson as the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sinning alone is different from leading many others to sin. Heaven does not help such a person do תשובה. This raises an obvious question for the next step: what did גחזי do to make others sin?

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition
One who sins and causes the many to sin
He is not given the opportunity

steps.confusionAlert: גחזי is not saying that תשובה would be rejected. The teaching is that such a person is not given the chance (the help from Heaven) to do it.

phrases.english: Elisha said to him: Repent.
Gehazi said to him: This is what I received from you:
One who sins and causes the many to sin
is not given the chance to do repentance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why אלישע's attempt in step 6 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who sins and causes the many to sin is not given the opportunity to do תשובה.

steps.title: What did גחזי do to make others sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what גחזי actually did that counted as causing the many to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he do?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next steps. The גמרא wants to know which act made גחזי someone who caused the many to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 put גחזי in the category of those who cause the many to sin, but never said what he did. The next three steps give three different answers.

phrases.english: What did he do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind גחזי's claim in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific act through which גחזי caused the many to sin.

steps.title: First answer: a magnet made ירבעם's calf float
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says גחזי used a magnetic stone to make ירבעם's golden calf hang in the air, so people thought it was a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: He hung a magnetic stone on ירבעם's sin and made it stand between heaven and earth.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to 'what did he do?' גחזי made the idol float in midair using a magnet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A floating idol looks like a miracle. That fake 'miracle' drew more people to serve the golden calf, so גחזי caused the many to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: ירבעם's sin, meaning the golden calf he set up for worship

phrases.english: There are those who say:
He hung a magnetic stone on Jeroboam's sin,
phrases.notes: 'ירבעם's sin' means the golden calf that ירבעם set up as an idol.

phrases.english: and made it stand between heaven and earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He made ירבעם's calf float in the air with a magnet.

steps.title: Second answer: the idol spoke words of the עשרת הדברות
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says גחזי engraved ה׳'s Name in the calf's mouth, and it spoke the first two of the Ten Commandments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: He engraved the Name in its mouth, and it would announce and say 'I am' and 'You shall not have.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to what גחזי did. He made the idol talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idol said the words 'I am ה׳ your God' and 'You shall not have other gods.' Hearing these holy words come from the calf made people trust it even more, so many more were led to sin.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
He engraved the Name in its mouth,
and it would announce and say
"I am" and "You shall not have."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:2–3, the first two of the Ten Commandments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from step 9 to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He engraved the Name in the calf's mouth so that it spoke 'I am' and 'You shall not have.'

steps.title: Third answer: גחזי pushed students away from אלישע
steps.stepSummary: A third opinion says גחזי kept the Rabbis away from אלישע. The proof is that only after he left did the students complain the place was too crowded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: He pushed the רבנן away from before him, as it says: 'And the בני הנביאים said to אלישע: Behold, the place where we sit before you is too narrow for us.' This implies that until now they were not many.
steps.whatsHappening: This third answer gives a different kind of sin: גחזי blocked people from learning תורה from אלישע. A פסוק is brought as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students complained that there was no room only in this later פסוק. The גמרא reads this to mean that before, there were few students, because גחזי was turning them away. Stopping many people from learning counts as causing the many to sin.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
He pushed the Rabbis away from before him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is אלישע. גחזי kept students from coming in to learn from him.

phrases.english: as it is said: "And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha:

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה [נָא] הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אֲנַחְנוּ יֹשְׁבִים שָׁם
phrases.english: Behold, please, the place where we sit
before you is too narrow for us,"
which shows that until now
they were not many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer, different in kind: blocking תורה learning instead of promoting idol worship.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He pushed the Rabbis away from learning before אלישע, as shown by the later crowding.
steps.raayaObject: That גחזי had been keeping students away
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 6:1: the place became too narrow only later

steps.title: Push away with the left, draw close with the right
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when pushing someone away, one should always also draw him close. It is a criticism of אלישע with גחזי and of יהושע בן פרחיה with ישו הנוצרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: Always let the left hand push away and the right hand draw close. Not like אלישע, who pushed גחזי away with both hands, and not like יהושע בן פרחיה, who pushed ישו הנוצרי away with both hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a lesson from a ברייתא about how to deal with a sinner or a failing student. It points to אלישע and יהושע בן פרחיה as examples of what not to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weaker hand (left) pushes, and the stronger hand (right) brings close, so the person never feels fully rejected. אלישע pushed גחזי away completely, and גחזי was lost. The same happened when יהושע בן פרחיה pushed away ישו הנוצרי.

keyTerms.meaning: With both hands, meaning total rejection

steps.whatToRemember: Even when you must distance someone, always leave a way back. Pushing away with both hands can make a person lost forever.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting guide for teachers and parents: correction must always come together with closeness.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
Always let the left hand push away
and the right hand draw close,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כֶּאֱלִישָׁע שֶׁדְּחָפוֹ לְגֵחֲזִי בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם,
phrases.english: not like Elisha, who pushed Gehazi away with both hands,
and not like Yehoshua ben Perachya
who pushed Yeshu the Nazarene away with both hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְעוֹלָם תְּהֵא שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a general lesson from how אלישע treated גחזי and adds a second example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Always push away with the left and draw close with the right, never rejecting someone with both hands.

steps.title: The פסוקים about גחזי taking נעמן's gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how אלישע pushed away גחזי by quoting the פסוקים in which גחזי takes silver from נעמן, lies about it, and is rebuked by אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The story of גחזי is as it is written: 'And נעמן said: Please take two talents, and he pressed him, and tied two talents of silver...' And: 'אלישע said to him: Where are you coming from, גחזי? He said: Your servant did not go anywhere. אלישע said: My heart did go along when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you. Is this the time to take silver, and clothing, and olive trees, and vineyards, and sheep, and cattle, and servants and maidservants?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the first story from the ברייתא in step 12, about how אלישע pushed away גחזי. It quotes the פסוקים from מלכים ב׳ פרק ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said that אלישע pushed גחזי away with both hands. Here the גמרא gives the source from תנ״ך. Notice the long list in אלישע's rebuke, because the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two talents, which are large weights of silver
Here or there, meaning anywhere at all

phrases.english: Gehazi, as it is written:
"And Naaman said: Please, take two talents,

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּפְרׇץ בּוֹ וַיָּצַר כִּכְּרַיִם כֶּסֶף וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and he pressed him, and tied two talents of silver, etc."
"And Elisha said to him: From where, Gehazi?

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא הָלַךְ עַבְדְּךָ אָנֶה וָאָנָה.
phrases.english: And he said: Your servant did not go anywhere.
And he said to him: Did my heart not go along

phrases.aramaic: כַּאֲשֶׁר הָפַךְ אִישׁ מֵעַל מֶרְכַּבְתּוֹ לִקְרָאתֶךָ
phrases.english: when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you?

phrases.aramaic: הַעֵת לָקַחַת אֶת הַכֶּסֶף וְלָקַחַת בְּגָדִים
phrases.english: Is it the time to take the silver, and to take clothing,
and olive trees, and vineyards, and sheep, and cattle,
and servants and maidservants?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first example mentioned in the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוקים show that גחזי took silver from נעמן and was rebuked by אלישע with a long list of eight kinds of things.

steps.title: Did גחזי really take all those things?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that גחזי only took silver and clothing, so why does אלישע list olives, vineyards, animals and servants?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he really take all of that? He only took silver and clothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the wording of the פסוק. אלישע's list is much longer than what גחזי actually took.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself says גחזי took only two talents of silver and two changes of clothes. So the extra items in the list seem out of place. The גמרא needs an explanation for why אלישע named all eight things.

phrases.english: And did he take all of this?
It was silver and clothing that he took!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the long list in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of eight items in אלישע's rebuke (מלכים ב׳ 5:26)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גחזי only took silver and clothing, so mentioning olives, vineyards, animals and servants seems not to fit.

steps.title: רבי יצחק tells the full story of נעמן's healing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that אלישע was teaching about the eight שרצים at the time. He tells how נעמן was healed in the ירדן, how אלישע refused his gifts, and how גחזי secretly took some and hid them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: At that time אלישע was sitting and teaching about the eight שרצים. נעמן, the general of the king of ארם, had צרעת. A young girl who had been taken captive from ארץ ישראל told him: If you go to אלישע, he will heal you. When he came, אלישע told him: Go dip in the ירדן. נעמן said: Are you making fun of me? The people with him said: What do you lose? Go try it. He went and dipped in the ירדן and was healed. He came and brought אלישע everything he had with him, but אלישע would not take it. גחזי left אלישע, went and took what he took, and hid it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק starts answering the question by telling the background story. He opens with a detail that will matter at the end: אלישע was teaching about the eight שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening detail about the eight שרצים is the key to the answer. The rest of the story sets up how גחזי got the silver: אלישע refused נעמן's gifts, and גחזי went behind his back to take them.

keyTerms.meaning: The eight creeping creatures that are טמא, listed in ויקרא פרק י״א
A person with צרעת, a skin disease
Are you making fun of me?
And he put it away, hid it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
At that time Elisha was sitting
and teaching about the eight creeping creatures.
Naaman, general of the army of the king of Aram,
had tzaraas.
A certain young girl said to him,
who had been taken captive from the Land of Israel:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָזְלַתְּ לְגַבַּי אֱלִישָׁע מַסֵּי לָךְ.
phrases.english: If you go to Elisha, he will heal you.
When he came, he said to him:
phrases.notes: Here אלישע is the one speaking to נעמן.

phrases.english: Go dip in the Jordan.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַחוֹכֵי קָא מְחַיְּיכַתְּ בִּי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are you making fun of me?
Those who were with him said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי נָפְקָא לָךְ מִינַּהּ? זִיל נַסִּי.
phrases.english: What difference does it make to you? Go try it.
He went and dipped in the Jordan and was healed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא אַיְיתִי לֵיהּ כֹּל הָנֵי דְּנָקֵיט.
phrases.english: He came and brought him all the things he had with him.
He did not want to accept them from him.
Gehazi took leave from before Elisha,
went, took what he took, and put it away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הָיָה אֱלִישָׁע יוֹשֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 14 by telling the background story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The background: אלישע was teaching the eight שרצים when גחזי went and secretly took נעמן's gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Background to the resolution: אלישע was teaching the eight שרצים when גחזי secretly took נעמן's gifts, which sets up why eight items are listed.

steps.title: גחזי's reward for the eight שרצים and his punishment
steps.stepSummary: אלישע sees צרעת on גחזי's head and says, 'Wicked one, the time has come to take your reward for the eight שרצים.' That is why he listed eight items. Then he curses גחזי with נעמן's צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When גחזי came back, אלישע saw צרעת sprouting on his head. He said to him: Wicked one! The time has come to take the reward for the eight שרצים. 'And the צרעת of נעמן will cling to you and your children forever, and he left him with צרעת as white as snow.'
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the answer to step 14. The eight items in אלישע's list match the eight שרצים he was teaching about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גחזי took the money while אלישע was teaching the eight שרצים. So אלישע told him he had taken his reward for that learning in this world. The list of eight things (silver, clothing, olive trees, vineyards, sheep, cattle, servants, maidservants) matches the eight שרצים, even though גחזי only took silver and clothing.
steps.whatToRemember: The eight items in אלישע's rebuke match the eight שרצים he was teaching when גחזי took the money. גחזי was punished with נעמן's צרעת for himself and his children.

phrases.english: When he came, Elisha saw the tzaraas
that was sprouting on his head.
He said to him: Wicked one!

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעַ עֵת לִיטּוֹל שְׂכַר שְׁמֹנָה שְׁרָצִים.
phrases.english: The time has come to take the reward for the eight creeping creatures.
"And the tzaraas of Naaman will cling to you and to your children forever,
and he went out from before him with tzaraas, white as snow."

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ עֵת לִיטּוֹל שְׂכַר שְׁמֹנָה שְׁרָצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יצחק's story and directly resolves the question about the eight items.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלישע listed eight items because גחזי took his reward for learning the eight שרצים.
steps.terutzMaskana: אלישע listed eight items, even though גחזי took only silver and clothing, because גחזי was taking his reward for learning the eight שרצים.

steps.title: The four מצורעים were גחזי and his sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the four lepers at the city gate mentioned later in מלכים were גחזי and his three sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And there were four men with צרעת at the entrance of the gate.' רבי יוחנן said: These were גחזי and his three sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a related teaching. He identifies the four lepers in a later פסוק as גחזי and his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע's curse said the צרעת would cling to גחזי 'and to your children.' רבי יוחנן shows the curse came true, because גחזי and three sons appear together as lepers.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance of the city gate

phrases.english: "And there were four men with tzaraas at the entrance of the gate" —
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Gehazi and his three sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גֵּחֲזִי וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the curse in step 16 on גחזי's children was carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four lepers at the gate were גחזי and his three sons.

steps.title: What was the story with יהושע בן פרחיה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the second example from the ברייתא and asks what happened with יהושע בן פרחיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story of יהושע בן פרחיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next story. Now it turns to the second example in the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said יהושע בן פרחיה pushed away ישו with both hands. The גמרא now asks for the details, and the answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Yehoshua ben Perachya, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the גחזי story and goes back to the second example of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The details of how יהושע בן פרחיה pushed away ישו.

steps.title: יהושע בן פרחיה flees to אלכסנדריא and is called back
steps.stepSummary: When ינאי המלך killed the Rabbis, יהושע בן פרחיה and ישו ran away to אלכסנדריא in מצרים. When peace came, שמעון בן שטח sent a letter calling him home.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ינאי המלך was killing the Rabbis, יהושע בן פרחיה and ישו went to אלכסנדריא in מצרים. When there was peace, שמעון בן שטח sent him a message: From me, ירושלים the holy city, to you, אלכסנדריא of מצרים: My sister, my husband is staying with you, and I sit alone and abandoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling the story of יהושע בן פרחיה. This part is only the background. Steps 20–22 tell the rest of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter is written as if ירושלים were a wife whose husband went away. The 'husband' is יהושע בן פרחיה, the leading Torah scholar, and ירושלים is empty without him. This explains why he left אלכסנדריא with ישו, which leads to what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: King ינאי, a חשמונאי king who killed the Rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: The letter is not from a real woman. ירושלים is described as a wife, and the 'husband' is יהושע בן פרחיה, whom the city needs back.

phrases.english: When King Yannai was killing the Rabbis,
Yehoshua ben Perachya and Yeshu went
to Alexandria of Egypt.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה שְׁלָמָא, שְׁלַח לֵיהּ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח:
phrases.english: When there was peace, Shimon ben Shatach sent to him:
From me, Jerusalem the holy city,
to you, Alexandria of Egypt:
My sister, my husband is staying in your midst,
phrases.notes: 'My husband' means יהושע בן פרחיה, the great Torah leader ירושלים is missing.

phrases.english: and I sit desolate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 18 with the background of the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Background: יהושע בן פרחיה and ישו ran away to אלכסנדריא, and שמעון בן שטח later called him back to ירושלים.

steps.title: The remark at the inn and the נידוי
steps.stepSummary: On the way home, יהושע בן פרחיה praises an inn. ישו takes the word to mean the innkeeper's wife and comments on her eyes. His teacher rebukes him and puts him in נידוי with four hundred shofars.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got up and set out, and he came to a certain inn. They treated him with great honor. He said: How beautiful is this inn! ישו said to him: My teacher, her eyes are narrow. He said to him: Wicked one! Is this what you busy yourself with? He brought out four hundred shofars and put him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story from Step 19. יהושע בן פרחיה heads home, and a misunderstanding at an inn leads him to put his student ישו in נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אַכְסַנְיָא can mean the inn or the woman who runs it. יהושע בן פרחיה meant the inn and the hospitality. ישו heard it as praise of the woman's looks and answered by criticizing her eyes. The teacher saw that as improper attention to a married woman, so he punished him very harshly.

keyTerms.meaning: An inn, a place where guests stay
An inn, or the woman who runs it (both meanings matter in this story)
He put him in נִידּוּי (excommunicated him)

phrases.aramaic: קָם, אֲתָא, וְאִתְרְמִי לֵיהּ הָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא.
phrases.english: He got up and set out, and he happened upon a certain inn.
They treated him with great honor.
He said: How beautiful is this inn!
phrases.notes: אַכְסַנְיָא can mean the inn or the woman who runs it. The whole story turns on that double meaning.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher, her eyes are narrow.
phrases.notes: This is ישו speaking. He took his teacher's words as talking about the innkeeper's wife.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רָשָׁע! בְּכָךְ אַתָּה עוֹסֵק?
phrases.english: He said to him: Wicked one! Is this what you busy yourself with?
He brought out four hundred shofars and put him in נידוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָם, אֲתָא, וְאִתְרְמִי לֵיהּ הָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after receiving the letter from שמעון בן שטח, יהושע בן פרחיה travels home.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened with יהושע בן פרחיה (asked in Step 18)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the trip home he put ישו in נידוי for an improper remark.

steps.title: The misread hand signal
steps.stepSummary: ישו asks several times to be taken back, and his teacher ignores him. One day during קריאת שמע the teacher decides to accept him and waves his hand. ישו thinks he is being rejected for good, and he sets up a brick and bows to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישו came before him several times and said: Accept me! He paid no attention to him. One day he was reciting קריאת שמע, and ישו came before him. He intended to accept him, and he signaled to him with his hand. ישו thought: He is pushing me away. He went, stood up a brick, and bowed down to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its turning point. A hand signal meant as 'wait' is misread as 'go away,' and ישו turns to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher had finally decided to take ישו back. He could not speak because he was in the middle of קריאת שמע, so he used his hand. After being ignored so many times, ישו read the gesture as a final rejection. The earlier harshness is what made the misunderstanding so destructive.

keyTerms.meaning: He paid no attention to him
He signaled to him with his hand

phrases.english: He came before him several times,
and said to him: Accept me!
phrases.notes: Literally 'accept us.' He means: take me back as your student.

phrases.english: He paid no attention to him.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא קָרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: One day he was reciting קריאת שמע,
and ישו came before him.
He intended to accept him,
and he signaled to him with his hand.
phrases.notes: He couldn't talk in the middle of שמע, so he waved, meaning 'wait.'

phrases.english: But ישו thought: He is pushing me away.
He went, stood up a brick, and bowed down to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the נידוי: ישו's attempts to come back and how they failed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened with יהושע בן פרחיה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His harsh rejection led ישו to misread a signal and turn to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Too late to come back
steps.stepSummary: When the teacher tells ישו to come back, ישו answers with his teacher's own teaching: someone who sins and causes the public to sin is not given the chance to do תשובה. The גמרא adds that ישו did sorcery and led Israel astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Come back! ישו said to him: This is what I received from you: Whoever sins and causes the many to sin is not given the chance to do תשובה. And the Master said: ישו practiced sorcery, incited, and led Israel astray.
steps.whatsHappening: This step ends the story. ישו refuses to return, and the גמרא says he went on to lead others astray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישו quotes the rule that one who causes the many to sin is not helped to do תשובה. He uses it to claim it is already too late for him. The added line from 'the Master' shows how far it went: he led many people astray. This is the outcome the ברייתא warned about when it said not to push away 'like יהושע בן פרחיה.'

keyTerms.meaning: One who sins and causes the many to sin
He is not given the chance (from Above)
Incited and led astray (toward עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה)

steps.whatToRemember: The story of יהושע בן פרחיה illustrates the earlier ברייתא: pushing someone away with both hands, with no door left open, can lose them completely.

phrases.english: He said to him: Come back (do תשובה)!
He said to him: This is what I received from you:
Whoever sins and causes the many to sin
is not given the chance to do תשובה.
And the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁוּ כִּישֵּׁף וְהֵסִית וְהִדִּיחַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: ישו practiced sorcery, incited, and led Israel astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story begun in Step 19, showing the final result of the rejection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened with יהושע בן פרחיה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישו refused to return and went on to lead many Jews astray.

steps.title: Left hand pushes, right hand draws close
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that with the יצר, a child, and a woman, one should push away with the weaker left hand and draw close with the stronger right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: With the יצר, a child, and a woman, let the left hand push away and the right hand draw close.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא that gives the general rule behind the stories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weaker left hand pushes away and the stronger right hand draws close, so the drawing close should be the stronger force. With the יצר, a child, or one's wife, you sometimes need to hold back, but you should never reject completely. This rule is exactly what יהושע בן פרחיה and אלישע did not follow.
steps.whatToRemember: Discipline should be gentler than closeness: push away with the weak hand, draw close with the strong hand.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said:
The evil inclination, a child, and a woman:
let the left hand push away and the right hand draw close.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories, the גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא that states the general principle they illustrate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Toward the יצר, a child, and a woman: push away with the left hand and draw close with the right.

steps.title: The three illnesses of אלישע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says אלישע fell ill three times: once for sending bears against the children, once for pushing away גחזי with both hands, and once with the illness he died from. The פסוק hints that there were earlier illnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: אלישע fell ill with three illnesses. One was because he sent bears against the children. One was because he pushed גחזי away with both hands. And one was the illness he died from, as it says: 'And אלישע fell ill with his illness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to אלישע and גחזי and teaches that אלישע himself was punished with illness for pushing גחזי away completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three illnesses, and one of them is directly tied to rejecting גחזי 'with both hands.' That links back to the warning about pushing away with two hands. The פסוק says 'his illness,' meaning the one that killed him, which suggests there were other illnesses before it.

keyTerms.meaning: He pushed him away with both hands (rejected him completely)
His illness (the one he died from)

steps.whyThisMatters: Even a great נביא like אלישע was held responsible for rejecting someone too harshly. This strengthens the lesson of 'the left hand pushes away and the right hand draws close.'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳלָאִים חָלָה אֱלִישָׁע –
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: אלישע fell ill with three illnesses:
one because he sent bears against the children,
and one because he pushed גחזי away with both hands,
and one that he died from,
[as it says: 'And אלישע fell ill with his illness, etc.']
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 13:14. Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; the corrected wording adds them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳלָאִים חָלָה אֱלִישָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the אלישע and גחזי story (Steps 15–17) to show that אלישע was punished for rejecting גחזי, matching the principle of Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלישע had three illnesses: for the bears, for pushing away גחזי with both hands, and the illness he died from.

steps.title: Before אברהם there was no visible old age
steps.stepSummary: Before אברהם, old and young looked the same. אברהם prayed for signs of old age, and the פסוק first calls someone old in connection with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until אברהם there was no aging. Anyone who saw אברהם said, 'That is יצחק,' and anyone who saw יצחק said, 'That is אברהם.' אברהם prayed for mercy that he would have old age, as it says: 'And אברהם was old, coming along in days.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last step spoke about אלישע's illnesses, the גמרא now brings a related teaching about 'firsts.' This step covers the first one: old age began with אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Father and son looked exactly alike, so people mixed them up. אברהם asked for old age so people could tell an older person apart. The proof is that 'זקן' is first said about אברהם in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Coming along in days; advanced in years

phrases.english: Until Abraham there was no aging.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל דְּחָזֵי לְאַבְרָהָם אֲמַר: הַאי יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: Anyone who saw Abraham said: That is Isaac.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל דְּחָזֵי לְיִצְחָק אָמַר: הַאי אַבְרָהָם.
phrases.english: Anyone who saw Isaac said: That is Abraham.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא אַבְרָהָם רַחֲמֵי דְּלֶיהְוֵי לֵיהּ זִקְנָה,
phrases.english: Abraham prayed for mercy that he should have old age,
as it is stated: “And Abraham was old, well along in days.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 24's mention of אלישע's illnesses with a list of 'firsts'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Visible old age began with אברהם, in answer to his prayer.

steps.title: Before יעקב there was no illness
steps.stepSummary: Before יעקב, people did not get sick before dying. יעקב prayed, and illness began.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until יעקב there was no weakness. He prayed for mercy and there was weakness, as it says: 'And someone said to יוסף: Behold, your father is ill.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second 'first.' Illness before death began with יעקב, who prayed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יעקב, people did not grow weak before they died. The proof is the פסוק about יעקב, 'Behold, your father is ill,' which the גמרא treats as the first time illness appears.

phrases.english: Until Jacob there was no weakness,
he prayed for mercy and there was weakness,
as it is stated: “And one said to Joseph: Behold, your father is ill.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the same list of 'firsts'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Illness before death began with יעקב, in answer to his prayer.

steps.title: Before אלישע no sick person ever recovered
steps.stepSummary: Before אלישע, anyone who got sick died from it. אלישע prayed and recovered, and the פסוק hints at this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until אלישע there was no sick person who recovered. Then אלישע came, prayed for mercy, and recovered, as it says: 'And אלישע fell ill with his illness from which he would die.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third 'first,' and it brings us back to אלישע. He was the first person to get sick and then get better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the illness from which he would die.' That wording means he had earlier illnesses he did not die from. So he must have recovered from them, which ties back to the illnesses listed in step 24.
steps.whatToRemember: Three 'firsts': old age began with אברהם, illness before death with יעקב, and recovering from illness with אלישע. Each one came through prayer.

phrases.aramaic: עַד אֱלִישָׁע לָא הֲוָה אִינִישׁ חָלֵישׁ דְּמִיתְּפַח,
phrases.english: Until Elisha there was no sick person who recovered,
and Elisha came and prayed for mercy and recovered,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וֶאֱלִישָׁע חָלָה אֶת חׇלְיוֹ אֲשֶׁר יָמוּת בּוֹ״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: “And Elisha fell ill with his illness from which he was to die.”

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד אֱלִישָׁע לָא הֲוָה אִינִישׁ חָלֵישׁ דְּמִיתְּפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final item, which closes the discussion of אלישע's illnesses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Recovery from illness began with אלישע, in answer to his prayer.

steps.title: דור המבול has no share in עולם הבא and will not stand in judgment
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. דור המבול has no חלק לעולם הבא and will not even stand in judgment. This is learned from 'לא ידון רוחי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: דור המבול has no share in עולם הבא, and they will not stand in judgment, as it says: 'My spirit shall not judge with man forever.' That means no judgment and no spirit.
steps.whatsHappening: The story section is over, and a new משנה starts. It lists groups with no חלק לעולם הבא, beginning with דור המבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reads 'ידון' as connected to 'דין' (judgment), and 'רוחי' as the soul. So דור המבול will neither be judged nor get their souls back at the end of days.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the flood (נח's time)
A share in the World to Come
Stand in judgment at the end of days
Will judge; read here as related to דין

phrases.english: MISHNA: The generation of the flood
have no share in the World-to-Come,
and they do not stand in judgment,
as it is stated: “My spirit shall not abide [yadon] in man forever”
meaning: neither judgment nor spirit.
phrases.notes: 'ידון' points to judgment, and 'רוחי' points to the soul. They get neither one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the אגדה about אלישע
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דור המבול loses עולם הבא and is not even brought to judgment.

steps.title: דור הפלגה has no share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: דור הפלגה has no חלק לעולם הבא. The פסוק speaks of scattering twice: once for this world and once for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: דור הפלגה has no share in עולם הבא, as it says: 'And ה׳ scattered them from there over the face of all the earth,' and it is also written: 'And from there ה׳ scattered them.' The first 'scattered them' is in this world. The second 'from there ה׳ scattered them' is for עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to the second group: the people who built the tower of בבל (דור הפלגה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה mentions their scattering twice in a row. The משנה says a repeat is not extra words. One scattering is their punishment in עולם הזה, and the other is their being pushed away from עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the dispersion (the tower of בבל)

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹר הַפְּלַגָּה אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: The generation of the dispersion has no share in the World-to-Come,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיָּפֶץ ה׳ אֹתָם מִשָּׁם עַל פְּנֵי כׇל הָאָרֶץ״,
phrases.english: as it is stated: “And the Lord scattered them from there upon the face of all the earth,”
and it is written: “And from there He scattered them.”
“And the Lord scattered them”: in this world,
“and from there the Lord scattered them”: for the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוֹר הַפְּלַגָּה אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second group in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דור הפלגה loses עולם הבא, based on the doubled scattering in the פסוק.

steps.title: אנשי סדום have no share in עולם הבא but will stand in judgment
steps.stepSummary: אנשי סדום have no חלק לעולם הבא, learned from 'רעים' and 'חטאים.' But unlike דור המבול, they will stand in judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אנשי סדום have no share in עולם הבא, as it says: 'And the men of סדום were wicked and sinners before ה׳ exceedingly.' 'Wicked' is in this world, and 'sinners' is for עולם הבא. But they do stand in judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the third group, אנשי סדום. It adds that they will still stand in judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two describing words, 'רעים' and 'חטאים,' are split between עולם הזה and עולם הבא. The word 'אבל' sets them apart from דור המבול. They lose עולם הבא, but they are still brought to judgment.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two separate outcomes. Having no חלק לעולם הבא is one thing, and not standing in judgment is another. Here, אנשי סדום lose עולם הבא but are still judged, while דור המבול loses both.

phrases.aramaic: אַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: The people of Sodom have no share in the World-to-Come,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם רָעִים וְחַטָּאִים לַה׳ מְאֹד״
phrases.english: as it is stated: “And the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly”
“wicked”: in this world,
“and sinners”: for the World-to-Come.
But they do stand in judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third group in the list, with a contrast to דור המבול on judgment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנשי סדום lose עולם הבא but will stand in judgment.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: neither group stands in judgment
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה disagrees with the last ruling. He holds that both groups do not stand in judgment, and he begins quoting a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: Both these and those do not stand in judgment, as it says: 'Therefore [the wicked] shall not rise...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה argues with the תנא קמא. He says אנשי סדום, like דור המבול, will not stand in judgment. His proof פסוק continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא made a difference between דור המבול and סדום. רבי נחמיה erases that difference and treats both the same. His source is a פסוק saying the wicked will not 'rise' in judgment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Neḥemya says:
Both these and those do not stand in judgment,
phrases.notes: He means the people of סדום and דור המבול together.

phrases.english: as it is stated: “Therefore the wicked shall not stand
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:5. The rest of the פסוק comes right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ אֵין עוֹמְדִין בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the משנה, against the 'אבל עומדין בדין' ruling for סדום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, אנשי סדום also will not stand in judgment, just like דור המבול.
